parent_latest_release.name: Strata v0.1.41
parent_latest_release.body: **Faster on more than one GPU, faster short prompts on NVIDIA, about twice as fast prompts on Windows with little RAM, and a long list of fixes.** Two defaults change: `--batch` on a layer split now runs one pipeline group per GPU, and short prompt chunks on one NVIDIA GPU get help from the CPU (this one changes the last bits of an answer; one setting turns it off). Update with `UPDATE.bat` (Linux: `./update.sh`); setup replaces the engine with 0.1.41. This release includes the Pascal decode fix from 0.1.40.4. ## Speed Against 0.1.40.4, default settings, interleaved pairs, medians (prompt = time to read it; higher is better in every column): | Machine, model | Prompt 512 / 1K tokens | Prompt 4K / 20K | Decode | |---|---|---|---| | RTX 3060 12 GB, Linux, IQ3_XXS | +28% / +22% | equal | equal | | Tesla P100 16 GB, Linux, IQ3_XXS | +33% / +25% | equal | equal | | RTX 5070 12 GB, Windows, Q2_0 | equal* | equal | +0.4% (story +4.9%) | | RTX 5070, Windows, IQ3_XXS / IQ3_S with a RAM budget | | +16% / +23-25% | +3% | | 1x Radeon AI PRO R9700, Linux, Q2_0 | equal | equal | equal | | Arc Pro B70 32 GB, Linux, IQ3_S | +13% / +12% | +10% / +10% | equal | | Arc A750 8 GB, Linux, IQ3_XXS | equal | equal | equal | \* On the RTX 5070 with Q2_0, setup's automatic expert cache already holds about 3,700 experts on the card, so the CPU has almost nothing to take during a short prompt; with a smaller cache (`--expert-cache 1500`) the same prompts are 15-27% faster. Answers in every row are identical to 0.1.40.4 with `STRATA_PREFILL_CPU_SHARE=0` (Q2_0, IQ3_XXS, Coder and IQ3_S on the 5070, including 4K/20K-token prompts; IQ3_XXS on the 3060 and P100; Q2_0 on the R9700; the 10-prompt check on both Intel cards). - **Several clients on several GPUs (default; `--batch` with a layer split).** `--batch-groups auto` is now the default: every GPU stage works on its own group of requests at the same time, instead of one request group walking through the stages while the other cards wait. Total tokens per second at 8 clients: +32% to +68% (2, 3 and 4 GPUs; 4x Radeon AI PRO R9700 in the larger cases), with a better p95 as well. The answers are the same as with one group (the 8-request identity test passes on 2, 3 and 4 GPUs). `--batch-groups 1` turns it off. The first version of this slowed one long request that ran next to short ones by 39-47%; that is fixed and measured. The server also listens with a backlog of 256 now (`STRATA_HTTP_BACKLOG`): with 30 to 40 clients opening connections at once, some got "connection reset"; at 40 clients there are now 0 resets (134 tok/s in total on 4x R9700). The engine still serves 8 slots at a time (`--batch` above 8 is capped), so with 16 or more clients the rest queue. | 4x R9700, IQ3_S, `--batch 8` | 0.1.40.4 | 0.1.41 | |---|---|---| | 8 clients, total tok/s | 88 | 165 (+87%) | | 8 clients, finish p50 | 17.4 s | 9.3 s | | 40 clients, total tok/s | 88 | 153 (+75%) | | 40 clients, connection resets per run | 14-21 | 0 | - **Short prompts up to a third faster on one NVIDIA GPU (default, changes bits).** The CPU, idle while a prompt is read, takes part of the experts the GPU would otherwise stream, for chunks below 1,024 tokens (an agent's tool result, a short follow-up). It helps as much as the GPU has to stream: 0.1.41 against 0.1.40.4 reads a 512-token prompt 28% faster on an RTX 3060 and 33% faster on a Tesla P100 (1,000 tokens: 22% and 25%). On an RTX 5070 with Q2_0, setup's automatic cache already holds most of what a short prompt needs and the gain is 0-2%; with a smaller cache it is 15-27%. It is never slower in our runs. Longer prompts are unchanged. **The answers can differ slightly from 0.1.40.4**: first-token KL against the share off averages 0.004 (max 0.025). `STRATA_PREFILL_CPU_SHARE=0` turns it off and gives the exact 0.1.40.x answers. Only one NVIDIA GPU without `--batch` slots; layer splits, batch and AMD are as before. Thanks to sergqwer, whose measured on/off check this is. - **Windows, model bigger than RAM: prompts about twice as fast (#1323).** The prompt reader asks the drive for several experts in one request, and gives up the memory-mapped view of `experts.bin` once its reads bypass the cache (while it is mapped, Windows serves those reads one at a time). On the RTX 5070 PC the prompt time fell 45-52%, with the same tokens in 18 of 18 runs; in the release check, IQ3_XXS and IQ3_S with a RAM budget read 4K-20K prompts 16-25% faster on the same PC. On Linux the gain is small (3-4% with unbuffered reads, none through the page cache) and never a loss. Thanks to adonizm, whose #833 this is a port of, and to malloc32 for bringing it back. - **A prompt whose experts are already in RAM (#1353).** When the GGUF experts read in place are in the page cache (90% or more), the prompt reader uses its few-thread profile instead of the 32-thread SSD one, which had made RAM-resident prompts 4-7x slower for the reporter. On our 4x R9700 box (fast storage, 251 GB RAM) the old path was not slow to begin with, so we measured no change there (identical output); please tell us in #1353 what it does on yours. Where the engine cannot tell (Windows), it behaves as before; `STRATA_STAGER_SSD=0/1` forces either. - **Intel Arc Pro B70: the expert dequant writes in whole 16-byte runs.** 200 -> 423 GB/s of writes in the micro-benchmark, prompt +6%, output bit-identical. - **Intel Arc A750: decode 9.8 -> 12.0 tok/s (+22%).** The sampler no longer needs FP64, so the A-series FP64 emulation settings are not needed (docs/INTEL.md). - **Tokenizer cache.** A resent agent prompt (89K tokens) is encoded in 0.07 s instead of 0.32 s, the same ids. - **Automatic card order.** With an auto layer split, the faster card (more SMs x clock; on Linux AMD from the KFD topology) is put last, the order that measured faster in the reports that asked for it (#1352). `"gpu_order": "as_given"` keeps your order. Setup no longer writes `--remote-expert-opt` next to `--pipeline-windows` (the first turns the second off). The auto placement also sees each stage's PCIe link (#794, from shy). - **Prompt batches fill holes (#793):** a request takes a free slot below a busy one of its group first, so a request left alone goes back to the plain single-request path. ## Fixes - **A deadlock with `parallel: 2` fixed.** Long, long, short requests could hang forever: a request waiting for a slot gave back nothing while it waited, and the slot a paused read held needed those lines. - **A full conversation cache evicts old entries to pass the RAM check instead of dropping the snapshot** (#1347; a conversation that holds a pinned shared prefix is never evicted this way). Thanks to alanthinker. - **Hung engines (#1317, #1407).** A request whose engine prints nothing for 90 s, uses no CPU, moves no disk bytes and has an idle GPU is ended and restarted (`STRATA_ENGINE_STALL_S`, 0 turns it off; needs `psutil`, which setup installs). An engine that is silent but working is never ended by this. The prompt-stall watchdog now waits, up to 10 times its limit, while the OS is still reading the expert file (`STRATA_WATCHDOG_IO_S`, 0 turns it off); a real hang stops at the old limit. - **`CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1` hangs every verify window** (#1341, #1383): the engine now says so at start and in the stall report, with the variable named. Thanks to ischencheng. - **`--api-key` takes several keys** separated by commas, as llama.cpp does (#1344). - **`setup --calibrate` keeps its earlier measurements** when a later engine start fails; it drops that candidate and goes on (#1337). The PCIe sweep no longer ends at 1.0 and visits each value once per round (#1332, #1345, from aly8246). - **A config with a `vision` section but no `--vision` in its args** now starts the engine with images (#1322). - **Tool calls written ``** are read as the call NAME (#1430). The vision encoder's start error now names the busy or unavailable GPU, and setup warns about a non-Default compute mode (#1445). - **q8_1 scale overflow** at the three remaining emit sites is clamped like the others (#1448); default answers unchanged. - **Intel B70, two cards (#1440):** the host mirror keeps to the first stage's layers and the free-memory estimate no longer subtracts the same VRAM twice; a single card is unchanged (11,338 cache slots as before). The doorbell spin bound is chosen per device at run time (#1397; no gain measured on a Linux B70, Windows keeps 2,000,000 reads). - **Prompt buffers (#1454, #1465):** the half output shares the embedding storage (320 MiB less at 32,768 rows) and the hyper-connection norm products stay in existing scratch. Default answers are identical; `STRATA_EMB_REUSE_ACCOUNT=1` lets the planner use the saved bytes (below). - **Batch MTP** with a shared draft head (#1329); a gfx906 build that compiles again (#1396); the engine links against the toolkit whose `nvcc` builds it (#1359). - **Server:** a malformed body gets a 400 with the traceback in the log; bodies over 256 MiB (`STRATA_MAX_BODY_MIB`) and a bad Content-Length are refused before they are read; the engine warns when `--batch-groups` is used with `--batch-mtp`. - **#795 (crash on a CPU without AVX-512):** we could not find a software cause, so this is hardening, not a claimed fix. The AVX-512 probe and the "is this format supported" helpers are out of the wide-instruction files, and the tests now disassemble the kernels and run the CPU tests under Intel SDE, so a wide instruction on an AVX2 path fails the build. - **AMD:** a warning when the long-prompt path's lend coverage is short, and the method behind a 925 -> 2,503 tok/s prompt on an RX 7900 XTX is in docs/AMD_HIP.md (#1389, from zhhhn); hipBLASLt tuning tables for gfx1151 (alexdns1, #1388) and gfx1150 / Radeon 890M (#1395, 1.5-1.7x prompts in the author's runs; we cannot measure either card); `STRATA_PREFILL_STREAM_MIN=128` in the gfx1151 fast configuration (#1391). - **Tooling:** `strata --version`; setup prints "checksum verified"; update scripts drop their backup branch when the move fails; fewer build warnings; test fixes; `tools/serve_load.py`, a load generator for the server. Docs: Windows "Lock pages in memory" takes effect at the next logon (#1412), the V100 notes, ten community benchmark folders and more. ## New opt-in switches None of these changes the default. - **`--peer-device` prompt share without P2P (#1251).** Most GeForce pairs have no P2P, and the prompt share used to refuse them. It now goes through pinned host memory, with per-token sums sent back in FP16. On 4x R9700 with P2P forced off, IQ3_S: prompt 690 -> 737 tok/s at 4K (+6.9%) and 1,353 -> 1,515 at 32K (+12%), but decode was 4-5% slower in those cases and the answers change bits, so it is off by default. First-token KL against the old path over 12 prompts: 0.009 mean with FP16 sums (11 of 12 top tokens the same), 0.005 with FP32, and 0 (bit-identical) when whole rows are sent instead of sums; with P2P available nothing changes. Thanks to Thig, whose work this is, built on Eddoursul's second-GPU prompt path. - **`STRATA_GDN_CHUNKED=1` (#1372).** The DeltaNet recurrence of the prompt in 32-token chunks, for cards with 128 SMs (sergqwer measured 1.8x there). We have no such card; on 48 and 28 SMs it is slower (0.87x and 0.73x), so `=1` does nothing below 128 SMs. Other bits (KL 0.002-0.009 on the cards we forced it on). - **Foresight swap space (`STRATA_FS_SLOTS`, #1348).** Per-layer VRAM slots filled with recently missed experts. In our runs it was 0.91-1.00 of the default decode speed on an RTX 3060, a Tesla P100 and an RTX 5070, so it stays off; it may pay on a single 24 GB card with many misses per layer, which we do not have. - **`STRATA_ROUTE_RESIDENT` (experimental).** Routing that prefers experts already in the cache, in verify windows. It changes the answers (KL 0.07 at margin 0.5). RTX 5070 Q2_0: +4.1% decode (6 of 6 pairs). RTX 3060 IQ3_XXS: -0.1% and -1.6%, because the draft's acceptance on code drops. Try it on a 12-24 GB card with a Q2_0 pack, and measure; do not expect a win everywhere. - **`STRATA_EMB_REUSE_ACCOUNT=1`.** The prompt planner counts the VRAM the shared buffer saved, so a VRAM-limited card gets a slightly larger chunk (RTX 3060 6,400 -> 6,656 tokens, about +3.9% prompt speed). It changes the prompt's rounding, so it is off. - **`STRATA_ADAPT_LAG=2`.** The adaptive tier's copies are waited for one window later. Tesla P100 +3.5% (6 of 6), RTX 5070 +0.2%, RTX 3060 -1.3%; opt-in. - **`STRATA_SM70_TABLE=1` (#1401).** The V100 decode kernels from rewin123 and NoxestNoz, with a per-architecture rows table. We have no V100; they become the default once measured on one. - **The CPU share above 1,024 tokens, on a layer split and from mapped experts (#1414, from architectds).** Documented in docs/DETAILS.md with its numbers; in our check the 3,072-token extension was 2% slower at 2K on the RTX 5070, which is why the default stays below 1,024 tokens. `STRATA_PREFILL_CPU_SHARE_MAX=3072` turns the extension on. - **`STRATA_STAGE_PIN=1` (#1237, from ZhongUncle).** The buffers the expert cache is filled from are page-locked. Tesla P100 with RAM capped at 24 GB and `--mmap-experts`: 13.9 -> 15.0 tok/s (+8%). It was meant to be on by default, but the release check found IQ3_S answers corrupted after a 4,096-token prompt with it on (most likely a buffer reused before its copy finished), so it is off until that is fixed. Use it only to measure. ## Updating `UPDATE.bat` (Linux: `./update.sh`). Models and configs are not touched. If you want exactly the old answers on one NVIDIA GPU, put `"STRATA_PREFILL_CPU_SHARE": "0"` in the `"env"` block of your `strata-.json`. Thanks to everyone who reported, measured and sent patches; in particular sergqwer (the CPU share and the chunked recurrence), adonizm (batched reads for Windows), Thig (the no-P2P prompt share), paulhothersall and lineape (the bisect behind the Pascal fix), and mlfather (the engine review that started the multi-GPU concurrency work). --- Strata is free and open source. If it runs well on your PC, a coffee keeps the work on it going:

parent_mac_issue.title: Milestone: Add Apple Silicon Cross-Platform Support
parent_mac_issue.body:
# Add macOS Apple Silicon Support

## Summary

Add native macOS support to **Strata**, targeting **Apple Silicon Macs only** (`arm64`, M1 and newer).

The goal is to make the existing project build, install, launch, and function correctly on macOS without attempting to support Intel Macs (`x86_64`).

## Scope

This issue should cover the work required to make Strata compatible with:

- macOS on Apple Silicon
- `arm64` architecture
- M1, M2, M3, M4, and newer Apple Silicon systems

Intel-based Macs are explicitly out of scope.

## Requirements

- [ ] Audit the current codebase for Windows/Linux-specific assumptions, APIs, paths, shell commands, dependencies, and build tooling.
- [ ] Replace or abstract platform-specific functionality where needed.
- [ ] Add macOS-compatible implementations for any OS-level functionality used by Strata.
- [ ] Ensure filesystem paths and configuration/storage locations follow macOS conventions.
- [ ] Update dependency handling for packages or native modules that do not currently support macOS ARM64.
- [ ] Ensure any bundled binaries or external executables have compatible `darwin-arm64` builds.
- [ ] Add or update build scripts so the project can produce a native Apple Silicon macOS build.
- [ ] Ensure development commands work correctly from a clean checkout on an M-series Mac.
- [ ] Document any macOS-specific prerequisites or setup steps.
- [ ] Preserve existing behavior on currently supported platforms wherever possible.

## Build Target

The macOS build only needs to target:

```text
darwin-arm64
```

Support for:

```text
darwin-x64
```

is not required.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Strata can be cloned and installed on a clean Apple Silicon Mac.
- [ ] All required dependencies install successfully on `arm64` macOS.
- [ ] The application builds successfully without architecture-related errors.
- [ ] The application launches and its primary functionality works on macOS.
- [ ] Platform-specific functionality either works natively on macOS or has an appropriate macOS implementation.
- [ ] No Rosetta 2 dependency is required for normal operation.
- [ ] A native `arm64` macOS build can be produced.
- [ ] macOS setup/build instructions are documented in the repository.
- [ ] Existing supported platforms are not unintentionally broken by the changes.

## Notes

The intent is **native Apple Silicon support**, rather than simply getting Strata to run through compatibility layers or Rosetta.

Where the project currently contains platform-specific logic, platform detection and isolated implementations should be preferred over duplicating large portions of the application.

Any functionality that cannot reasonably be supported on macOS should be identified and documented as part of the implementation.

parent_mac_comments.body: Out of scope: Strata has CUDA, HIP and SYCL backends and no Metal backend, so Apple Silicon is not supported. Closing; llama.cpp and MLX run these models on Macs.

llama_recent_prs.title: ggml: support non-contiguous SUM (CPU, CUDA, Vulkan)
llama_recent_prs.body:
## Overview

`test-backend-ops` includes `SUM(type=f32,ne=[33,256,1,1],permute=[1,0,2,3])`, which CUDA rejects and which crashes the CPU reference if enabled. Two small changes:
- CUDA: `supports_op` required `ggml_is_contiguous_rows`, but the kernel only requires `ggml_is_contiguously_allocated` (asserted in `ggml_cuda_op_sum` since #10544). The flat CUB reduction is valid for any gap-free view, since summation is order-independent. The `contiguous_rows` check was added in #16559 to keep CI green after that PR introduced permuted SUM test cases, it wasn't based on what the CUDA kernel can actually handle. This change makes `supports_op` match the condition the kernel itself asserts. The kernel is unchanged.
- CPU: `ggml_compute_forward_sum_f32` asserted `nb[0] == sizeof(float)`, so it aborted on non-contiguous rows, reached as soon as the CPU acts as reference (or fallback) for this case. Added a strided path keeping `ggml_float` accumulation; contiguous fast path unchanged. f16/bf16 variants left as-is.
- Vulkan: `supports_op` accepted SUM for any input with contiguous rows, but the kernel sums the tensor as a single flat block, so sliced views returned wrong results. Changed the check to `ggml_is_contiguously_allocated`, matching the CUDA fix (per 0cc4m’s go-ahead).

*Why CPU and CUDA together* : the CPU fix is required for the CUDA case to be testable, since the reference crashes once the case is enabled.

## Additional information

Testing (RTX 3070 Ti Laptop, CUDA 13.3):
- `test-backend-ops -o SUM`: 8/8, permuted case now passing
- Full `test-backend-ops`: 16094/16094
- `perf -o SUM`: unchanged

Ref #14909, #16559.

## Requirements

- I have read and agree with the [contributing guidelines](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- AI usage disclosure: YES. Used Claude for analysis help, code drafting for the CPU change, and the initial description draft. Reviewed, built, and tested locally.

llama_recent_prs.title: ggml : pipeline parallelism with MoE experts in host RAM
llama_recent_prs.body:
## Overview

Support pipeline parallelism with MoE experts in host RAM

## Additional information

When part of the MoE weights is in host RAM (`-ot`, `--cpu-moe`, `--n-cpu-moe`, or `fit` when the model does not fit in VRAM), llama.cpp turns pipeline parallelism off (`!has_tensor_overrides()` in llama-context.cpp). All the experts are then uploaded through the first device that can (GPU0 on CUDA) and the GPUs run strictly one after another.

This PR keeps pipeline parallelism working with the weights in host RAM. Each GPU uploads the experts of its own layers, consecutive ubatches overlap across devices. Long prompt processing is x1.5-2 faster on my 3x RTX PRO 4000, short prompts and generation stay about the same.

## Benchmarks

3x RTX PRO 4000 Blackwell (PCIe 5 x16, P2P), EPYC 9274F, 384 GB DDR5, CUDA 13.3. Common settings `-fa on -b 4096 -ub 4096 -lm none`, `CUDA_SCALE_LAUNCH_QUEUES=4x`. PP is for the 1st / 2nd request of a about 50k-token RFC 7540.

| setup | master | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Qwen3.8-Flash-Next Q8_0, server, fit preset | 1009 / 1019 | 1808 / 2102 |
| Qwen3.5-35B-A3B, `-ncmoe 999`, server | 2705 / 2725 | 5486 / 5901 |
| Qwen3.8, llama-bench fit, pp8192 / pp32768 / tg64 | 1464 / 1334 / 46.2 | 1749 / 2474 / 47.1 |
| Qwen3.5-35B-A3B fully in VRAM, server | 7659 / 8196 | 7520 / 8226 |
| DeepSeek-V4-Flash Q8, server, fit | 625 | 1128 |
| DeepSeek-V4-Flash Q8, llama-bench fit, pp32768 / tg128 | 711 / 24.0 | 1484 / 24.2 |

Commits:

1. **ggml : upload user inputs once per device before the splits.** In pipeline mode every graph input (KQ mask and friends) was copied `n_copies` times per device and the copies were held for the whole graph. Now one copy per device, uploaded async on the stream of the split that uses it. Alone it does not change the speed, but it cuts the compute buffers from 9133 to 2988 MiB per GPU (Qwen3.5-35B in VRAM, c=262144, and the saving grows with the context).

2. **llama : keep graph topology constant with pipeline parallelism.** With host weights the executed graph is not always the worst-case one, and then every ubatch of a prompt reallocated the compute buffers, which synchronizes all devices. So after a smaller graph the worst-case graph is reserved again. This is what makes the host-weights case fast at all: without this commit the branch gives 983/991 instead of 1809/2095 on the Qwen3.8 server bench.

3. **ggml : pipeline parallelism with weights in host memory.** The main part. One copy of a host weight per device instead of 4 held for the whole graph, the allocator reuses it between splits, each split backend writes it in stream order. Ops with host weights run on the device of their own layer through the graph callback, not all on GPU0. The pipeline is now enabled with overrides, but only when the host weights are spread over the devices - on the master `fit` layout (all host weights on the last GPU) it stays off and runs at master speed. Reading the MoE ids waits for the split backend and would stall the graphs in flight, so on large batches the whole expert tensor is uploaded instead (>= 16 ids per expert with a graph in flight, else a full batch with >= 64). Also fixes `ggml_backend_sched_reserve_size` to reset after `split_graph` so that the `fit` probes see the backend assignments made by the callback.

4. **common : balanced layer slices for fit with pipeline parallelism.** Master fit stacks all host weights on the last device (Qwen3.8 gets `-ts 7,4,38`), which is exactly the one-GPU upload this whole thing is about. When the pipeline conditions hold, fit now gives every GPU an equal slice of layers and converts them to full layers per device as they fit (`-ts 16,16,17`).

the CUDA top-k radix select from the earlier version of the branch is dropped, #28713 landed and already covers that path in master.

Corresponding discussion thread: #29964

## Requirements

- I have read and agree with the [contributing guidelines](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md)

## Overview

This commit adds a test for speculative rejection sampling test that excercises the speculative rejection sampling mechanism in common/speculative.cpp.

## Additional information

The motivation for this is have a test that verifies that the speculative draft models emitts tokens that  match the target models distribution. So when rejection sampling occurs it should still produce the same probability distribution as if we directly sampled from the target model.

Running the test:
```console
$ ctest --test-dir build -R "^test-speculative-rejection-sampling$" \
    --n_trials 5000 -V
```
This will generate two models, one target and one draft model.

For subsequent runs use the "fixture exclude any" option to avoid recreating the models:
```console
$ ctest --test-dir build-cpu-debug -R \
    "^test-speculative-rejection-sampling$" \
    -FA "^speculative-models$" --n_trails 5000 -V
```

llama_recent_prs.title: llama: keep the backend sampling graph static across ubatches
llama_recent_prs.body:
## Overview

As suggested by @ggerganov in #30216: fixes the server tests that abort with backend sampling in GGML_SCHED_NO_REALLOC builds (server-cuda, server-metal).

The reserve builds n_outputs_max_per_seq sampling chains per sampler, but a decode built one chain per output row (or one on the dummy row for an inactive sampler). In the draft test that is 549 nodes for the reserve against 417 for a decode: the first decode reallocates to the smaller graph, then the next decode with the same 417 nodes but one more output row needs a bigger out_ids, which is the "unexpected graph reallocation".

This takes option 1 to the end: every sampler always builds n_outputs_max_per_seq chains, the real rows first, the others on the padding row and not selected through ggml_build_forward_select, which inactive samplers already did. The reserve goes through the same build_sampling, so the graph keeps its topology for every ubatch, and graph_max_nodes counts exactly these chains. n_outputs_max_per_seq is 1 by default and in the server without speculative decoding, so the usual graph is unchanged.

## Additional information

Tested on CUDA with GGML_SCHED_NO_REALLOC=ON:
- test_slot_restore_checkpoints_draft_kv_type_change with backend sampling: abort -> pass
- tests.sh with and without LLAMA_ARG_BACKEND_SAMPLING=1: 417 passed each

llama_recent_prs.title: Fix CI: Fix models Backend webgpu by supporting GGML_OP_DUP
llama_recent_prs.body:
## Overview

Fix CI:
Models Backend webgpu-nvidia segfaults on master since #29622, on the very first model of test-llama-archs.

The new mixed batch path writes the token rows with set_rows into a ggml_dup of the embeddings. WebGPU had no GGML_OP_DUP, so the dup stayed on the CPU, while the set_rows writing in place into it was scheduled on WebGPU. WebGPU then got a destination living in a CPU buffer, read its context as a WebGPU buffer, and Dawn crashed. CUDA and Vulkan support DUP, so they never hit it.

DUP is the same copy as CPY and CONT, so it now goes through the same path and the whole mixed chain stays on WebGPU.

## Additional information

Tested on an RTX PRO 6000 through WebGPU with the CI Dawn build:
- test-llama-archs -s 1: segfault -> 160 rows, 0 FAIL
- test-backend-ops DUP 7/7, CPY 144/144, CONT 72/72

llama_recent_prs.title: vulkan: fold verify tokens and GQA heads into one flash-attention row…
llama_recent_prs.body:
> [!IMPORTANT]
> **WIP:** This is an Idea still in Development

## Overview

This RFC packs two query tokens and their GQA heads into one Vulkan coopmat1 flash-attention row tile, reusing KV data across each pair. Masks remain per-token and padding rows are not stored. The opt-in path covers GQA-6, 2–8 tokens, Br16, masked dense attention, zero ALiBi bias, and `split_k > 1`. Single-token decode and unsupported cases retain the original mapping.

## Benchmark Summary

- AMD Radeon PRO W7800 48 GB, `gfx1100` / RDNA3; Vulkan, RADV / Mesa `26.0.8-1ubuntu0.3`, f16 K/V
- Final revision `070dce136`, including the ALiBi guard, on base `c811cb8f0`
- Same-binary A/B: `GGML_VK_FA_QTOK_FOLD` unset → `1`; setting it to `0` also enables it

**Operation benchmark:** head sizes 256/256, 24 Q / 4 KV heads, four tokens, KV52480.

| Measurement | Fold off → on |
|---|---|
| `FLASH_ATTN_EXT`, median | 1072.1 → 562.8 µs (0.525× time; -47.5%) |

Two off runs and four on runs; fold-on timings ranged from 541.14 to 625.05 µs. Split-K also changes from 8 to 17, so this measures both token-pair reuse and changed work distribution.

**Server benchmark:** Qwen3.8 27B Q8_0 + MTP Q4_0 draft, same final revision.

- `--ctx-size 131072 -b 2048 -ub 2048 -ctk f16 -ctv f16 --flash-attn on --cache-ram 0`
- `--spec-type draft-mtp --spec-draft-n-max 3 --spec-draft-sampling probabilistic`
- One server arm per setting: a 57,594-token prefix followed by six seeded 256-token generations

| Measurement | Fold off → on |
|---|---|
| Generation time per estimated speculative step | 74.27 → 65.44 ms (-11.89%) |
| Generation throughput | 39.66 → 45.44 tokens/s (+14.57%) |
| Mean accepted length | 2.917 → 2.983 |

Step time is derived as `generation time / (draft tokens / 3)`. No accepted-length change was detected: relative-change CI95 [-4.85%, +9.20%].

**Testing and limits:**

- Final revision passes 5328/5328 FA cases off and on, including odd token counts, maskless and ALiBi fallbacks. GQA-6 coverage remains limited to head sizes 256/256, f16 K/V, and no sinks.
- The previously observed KV32768+ NMSE failures with folding both off and on remain unresolved; token-exact equivalence is not established.

## Requirements

llama_recent_prs.title: ggml-rpc: validate PAD_REFLECT_1D parameters
llama_recent_prs.body:
## Overview

This PR fixes a remote out-of-bounds write in the ggml RPC server when processing a malformed `PAD_REFLECT_1D` graph. It validates `PAD_REFLECT_1D` parameters at the RPC boundary and adds kernel-side assertions so invalid padding values cannot reach the memory write path.

Fixes #29914.

## Additional information

- The issue is triggered by untrusted `GRAPH_COMPUTE` messages. `rpc_server::deserialize_tensor()` copies `op` and `op_params` without validation.
- The fix rejects malformed `PAD_REFLECT_1D` nodes before execution and adds defensive assertions in `ggml_compute_forward_pad_reflect_1d()`.
- Regression coverage: `test-rpc-malformed-graph` covers the malformed graph case. A valid `PAD_REFLECT_1D` graph remains accepted.

llama_recent_prs.title: spec : zero-fill draft-cache holes left by mtmd chunks
llama_recent_prs.body:
## Overview

Fixes #27408. Follow-up to #28587.

With `--spec-type draft-dflash` and an mmproj model, every image request returns HTTP 500
(`failed to process speculative batch`). #28587 skips M-RoPE-pinned mtmd embedding batches in
the DFlash `process()` and assumes "the draft can jump over the gap" -- but that gap is not
harmless: the next token batch fails the draft KV cache's consecutive-position check. This
patch detects the per-sequence gap at the top of `process()` and seeds it with zero-feature
injections. Drafted tokens are still verified by the target, so output stays distribution-exact;
only draft acceptance immediately after an image is degraded.

## Additional information

- #28587 (merged) added the `pos_pinned` skip; this is the missing half that fills the resulting hole.
- The approach is due to @dagnarf (z-lab/llama.cpp-fork#1); this is the minimal port to upstream.
- Known remaining limitation noted in #27408: cross-request position gaps (non-consecutive
  positions spanning slots/requests) are not covered by this patch.
- Tested on 2x RTX 5060 Ti (CUDA, build b11434) with Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-Q4_K_M + mmproj-Q8_0 + a
  DFlash sidecar: image requests go from HTTP 500 to HTTP 200 with no `failed to process
  speculative batch` in the log; text-only n=6 quality is unchanged (paired bootstrap P = 0.505)
  and speed is within noise.
- No CI regression test is included: it would require a multimodal target + draft model in CI.

llama_recent_prs.title: graph : reorder get_rows for embeddings
llama_recent_prs.body: ## Overview cont #29622 fix #30033 With mixed batch support, we have 3 possible graph branches that produce the input embeddings: - from tokens referencing the token embeddings weight tensor - raw embeddings - mixed: both tokens + raw The way we currently implement it leads to interleaving graph ops (such as PAD, MUL, SCALE) with the token embeddings extraction (GET_ROWS). This is not desired because it creates unnecessary splits or leads to running some of the ops on the CPU. To fix that, we have to rework the logic such that it orders all GET_ROWS to be the first nodes in the graph. We can achieve this with the `ggml_build_forward_order`. The goal is SPLIT 0 to always contain just the GET_ROWS ops and nothing else: Before: After: TODO: - [ ] Refactor to make the implementation cleaner - [ ] Fix Gemma4 PLE - [ ] Fix a reshaped CPU tensor reaching the Meta backend (same as https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/29535#issuecomment-6017306253) ## Requirements - I have read and agree with the [contributing guidelines](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md) - AI usage disclosure: NO

llama_recent_prs.title: ui : add the models manager
llama_recent_prs.body:
## Overview

### Demo

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b27af954-0b36-4263-95df-edf95cadb4e3

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/dadcba6d-0892-42aa-b59b-73120d30ed65

### Features

- New **Manage models** dialog: one table of every model the server can serve — one row per repo with expandable quants, sections (loaded → downloading → favorites → local → hidden), sortable columns (name/context/status, sleep-aware), search and context/capability/modality filters (only modalities present are offered).
- Row actions in a drawer: favorite, load/unload, delete from disk, hide/unhide, download pause/resume; downloads get their own section with a progress bar; a partly hidden repo splits its quants across the hidden and local blocks.
- Model configuration pane as a side drawer: full model info and chat template, plus *Start a new chat* (loading the model first) / *Use in this chat* and load controls; on a phone the model information dialog stands in for the pane.
- Reworked model selector (`ModelsSelector`): owns the shared picker state and renders the desktop dropdown and the phone drawer as equal surfaces — provider-aware grouping, favorites and loaded pinned on top (listed once), hidden models filtered out, windowed lists with *show more*, provider mark + org avatar in the trigger; falls back to the manager on single-model servers, and a phone with one model still gets the drawer.
- Reasoning effort becomes its own control beside the selector with a fully transparent trigger (no background, no hover fill, any state); MCP servers move from the add menu to the sidebar rail.
- Mobile experience: add actions in a drawer (sharing its labels with the desktop dropdown via constants), floating model action bar, context gauge in a drawer.
- New settings: Hugging Face Hub metadata (off by default — no fetches and no avatars when off), group-models-by-family, capabilities-in-selector, org-name display (renamed + migrated).

### Architecture / logic

- New shared data layer: `modelsStore` composes list, selection, loading, recents (manual picks only), favorites, hidden and group-open state, all persisted to localStorage; status store feeds download progress (and the delete-from-disk action resolves through its cancel endpoint).
- HF Hub details cached per repo with request dedup (404s cached, failures retried; failed base-model lookups not cached), warmed for a capped slice (12) and fetched per row only near the viewport; local file paths never query the Hub; avatars load in CORS mode with a per-org retry cooldown, search icons ride the server's CORS proxy.
- Selector state derived in one hook, with the chat-form model concerns (conversation sync, modality tracking) extracted into `useChatFormModel`; both surfaces and the assistant-message badge share it.
- Shared model components extracted (avatar, capabilities, context, load control, row actions) reused by both surfaces; new UI primitives (drawer/sheet via `vaul-svelte`, toggles, collapsible sections, grouped list, near-viewport helper).
- `ModelOption` enriched with `contextLength`, `draftSidecars` (from `--model-draft` args) and chat-template-based capability fallback; family grouping, list windowing and manager helpers (`groupModelFamilies`, `groupModelQuants`, `splitHiddenQuants`, `hasActiveFilters`, `statusRank`) live in tested utils.
- Settings gained a versioned migration for the renamed org-name key; `tools/ui/README.md` documents the new structure and the drawer dependency.

llama_recent_prs.title: llama-server: Use reference-counted checkpoints instead of deep-copies
llama_recent_prs.body:
## Overview

<!-- Describe what this PR does and why. Be concise but complete -->
`llama-server` currently creates and reuses context-checkpoints through a vector copy.
Since the checkpoints are immutable by design, this patch introduces reference-counted sharing instead.

This PR includes 3 changes to the system:
- Use `std::shared_ptr` for the context checkpoints, allowing cheap (ref-counted) copies
- Skip zero-initialization - this _would_ be a security risk, but we ensure that the bytes are actually written
- Reject broken requests before inserting into the prompt cache, avoiding leakages and thrashing. This is cheap because it's just an `std::move`

## Additional information
This applies mainly to the host-side copies. The effects become larger as context grows. The effects are most visible when queuing events, as they need to wait on the serialized cache-checkpoint copies.
Tested on 3x Arc Pro B60, Threadripper 1950X x399 platform, 128GB RAM, qwen3.8-flash-next:UD-IQ4XS, RAM prompt cache 8GB, 16 checkpoints, checkpoint spacing 8192 tokens, no MTP, running on the SYCL backend (but should not affect this code).

llama_recent_prs.title: CUDA: permit quantizing into NVFP4 (Blackwell PP +40%)
llama_recent_prs.body:
## Overview This PR permits quantizing CUDA-native 4-bit float quants that leverage Blackwell's FP4 MMA for maximum speed. - a `Q4_0`-sized model - with `Q3_K` tier accuracy - and a nice 40% benchmark speedup (20% on longer prompts) ## Additional information ### Approach This is not a true NVFP4 quant, but rather NVFP4-backed quant: a true quant requires [two more levels of scaling, an orthogonal rotation (RHT), and so on](https://nvidia.github.io/TransformerEngine/features/low_precision_training/nvfp4/nvfp4.html) - quite a chore to implement all at once. And quite a headache to validate that every part works as intended in one go (merged in #21095). That said, it works and it is quite fast, to the point I keep returning to it. As `.scale`/`.input_scale` are optional (marked as `TENSOR_NOT_REQUIRED`) a `NVFP4.gguf` without them is a valid model file and the graph knows how to skips these scales. In other words, this primitive level of quantization is not a tech debt per se: a future version of `llama.cpp` is expected to be able to load it even if we later add the plumbing for `.input_scale`. With that said, I found that if I extend this work with another level of scaling and a quant-time MSE optimization, the final result edges towards `Q4_0` by mean KLD, but never approaches it, remaining between `Q3_K` and `Q4_0`. This early iteration is slightly worse (0.0895 KLD) than `Q3_K` (0.0826 KLD) - just a few lines of MSE (which I deliberately did not include to keep the diff small - see #23692) can push it over `Q3_K`. I also found that even a second level of scaling tanks the performance (-8%) due to the lack of a fused kernel, as per my best understanding. So instead of attacking these challenges upfront, I propose to start small and reap most benefits from this quant type, that is, better PP on Blackwell GPUs. | Mean KLD | Same
Top-P | Optimization / Baseline | Meaning | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 0.0343 | 93.05% | IQ4_XS baseline | | | 0.0486 | 91.71% | Q4_0 baseline | | | 0.0824 | 88.86% | Q3_K baseline | | | 0.0894 | 88.18% | NVFP4 | | | 0.0794 | 88.99% | quantize-time MSE scale search in `quantize_row_nvfp4_ref` | beats `Q3_K` KLD| | 0.0693 | 89.54% | per-tensor `.scale` with round-up | -8% pp, -5% tg but still under Q4_0 | | 0.0396 | 92.46% | f16 activations | 2.5x slower than Q4_0, KLD between Q4_0 and IQ4_XS | | 0.0712 | 89.92% | [calibrated Qwen3.6-27B-NVFP4](https://huggingface.co/unsloth/Qwen3.6-27B-NVFP4) | imported with #21095 | - Qs here are not imatrix-calibrated, so neither my NVFP4s. - For this test `unsloth/Qwen3.6-27B-NVFP4` has been imported as NVFP4/BF16 - By comparison NVFP4 is NVFP4 weights, Q6_K token embeddings, Q4_0 output. ### Testing Here's how you can test this out. You'll need a source BF16 GGUF for a dense model such as Qwen 3.6 27B. ``` python convert_hf_to_gguf.py Qwen3.6-27B --outtype bf16 --outfile qwen3.6-27b-bf16.gguf ``` Quantize: ``` llama-quantize qwen3.6-27b-bf16.gguf qwen3.6-27b-NVFP4.gguf NVFP4 llama-quantize qwen3.6-27b-bf16.gguf qwen3.6-27b-Q4_0.gguf Q4_0 llama-quantize qwen3.6-27b-bf16.gguf qwen3.6-27b-Q3_K.gguf Q3_K ``` And bench: ``` llama-bench -m qwen3.6-27b-Q3_K.gguf,qwen3.6-27b-Q4_0.gguf,qwen3.6-27b-NVFP4.gguf -r 10 -p 2048 -b 8192 -ub 4096 -fa 1 ``` My results on RTX 5090 after a warm-up round, rebased on top of b0df4c0: | model | size | test | t/s | |--------------------------|-----------|--------|-----------------| | qwen35 27B Q3_K - Medium | 12.56 GiB | pp2048 | 3455.00 ± 54.31 | | qwen35 27B Q3_K - Medium | 12.56 GiB | tg128 | 87.39 ± 0.71 | | qwen35 27B Q4_0 | 14.63 GiB | pp2048 | 4097.30 ± 72.95 | | qwen35 27B Q4_0 | 14.63 GiB | tg128 | 84.63 ± 0.40 | | qwen35 27B NVFP4 | 14.63 GiB | pp2048 | 5938.26 ± 26.29 | | qwen35 27B NVFP4 | 14.63 GiB | tg128 | 84.32 ± 0.75 | So 70% faster than a comparable `Q3_K` at the cost of extra 2 GiB. ### KLD results for qwen3.6-27b-NVFP4.gguf ``` ====== Perplexity statistics ====== Mean PPL(Q) : 7.104837 ± 0.079962 Mean PPL(base) : 6.793059 ± 0.075277 Cor(ln(PPL(Q)), ln(PPL(base))): 97.85% Mean ln(PPL(Q)/PPL(base)) : 0.044874 ± 0.002321 Mean PPL(Q)/PPL(base) : 1.045897 ± 0.002427 Mean PPL(Q)-PPL(base) : 0.311778 ± 0.016746 ====== KL divergence statistics ====== Mean KLD: 0.089473 ± 0.001813 Maximum KLD: 23.048244 99.9% KLD: 4.946882 99.0% KLD: 0.920187 95.0% KLD: 0.277249 90.0% KLD: 0.161836 Median KLD: 0.032971 10.0% KLD: 0.000863 5.0% KLD: 0.000238 1.0% KLD: 0.000037 0.1% KLD: 0.000004 Minimum KLD: -0.000010 ====== Token probability statistics ====== Mean Δp: -0.537 ± 0.037 % Maximum Δp: 99.898% 99.9% Δp: 59.771% 99.0% Δp: 20.307% 95.0% Δp: 8.959% 90.0% Δp: 5.187% 75.0% Δp: 1.016% Median Δp: -0.004% 25.0% Δp: -1.414% 10.0% Δp: -6.274% 5.0% Δp: -11.126% 1.0% Δp: -30.133% 0.1% Δp: -74.541% Minimum Δp: -99.916% RMS Δp : 8.445 ± 0.110 % Same top p: 88.176 ± 0.143 % ```

llama_recent_prs.title: metal: add the 128/96 flash attention kernels
llama_recent_prs.body:
## Overview

#30003 added flash attention tests with K = 128 and V = 96, and Metal crashed on them: it said it supported the pair, but had no kernel for it.

Instead of rejecting the pair (#30208), this adds the 128/96 kernels, the same way 96/64 is done (mma and vec, every K/V type Metal handles). supports_op now accepts exactly the pairs that have a kernel: K == V, plus 96/64, 128/96, 192/128, 320/256 and 576/512. The vec tuning baseline and the sparse path list get 128/96 too.

Tested on an M5 Max: test-backend-ops -o FLASH_ATTN_EXT passes 4973/4973 on Metal, the 128/96 cases run on Metal for every K/V type it supports, and 96/64, 192/128, 320/256 and 576/512 keep running on Metal. No model uses 128/96 yet, so the test suite and the CI are the coverage here.

## Additional information

Supersedes #30208
Follow-up #30003

llama_recent_prs.body:
I refactored and generalized the CUDA swizzling code a bit with support for strides that are not a multiple of 128 bytes as well as Volta and AMD. Still, I think we should keep them since they will be potentially useful in the future due to the reduced VRAM requirements.

The functions `load_ldmatrix_swizzled` and `load_ldmatrix_trans_swizzled` *could* become replacements for the non-`_swizzled` variants in the future since they are a superset of the functionality if the stride is known at compile time. However, I am not yet 100% sure about this so I'm avoiding mass-changing the kernels that use them for now.

llama_recent_prs.title: Multi-column on Intel XMX matrix engines refactored
llama_recent_prs.body:
## Overview

Multi-column (2 to 80 activation columns) mul_mat_vec_q for reordered K-quant and Q8_0 weights on the Intel XMX matrix engines (int8 DPAS, ESIMD), for the SYCL backend. It targets speculative decoding verification (2 to 8 tokens per step) and short prompt batches (9 to 80 tokens). Three types also use it for a single column (Q2_K, Q3_K, Q8_0).


## Additional information

The existing multi-column dp4a kernels redo the weight unpack and the per-column scale arithmetic for every column, so the cost grows with the batch size (about 5 lane operations per dp4a per extra column). Profiling showed the step time for 4 tokens was 46% above 1 token on a Q6_K model, and much worse for Q3_K. Decode of one token is bandwidth bound, speculative
verification is not, so this gap is important.

Hardware and setup: Intel Arc Pro B70 (32 GB), Windows 10, oneAPI 2026.1 (icx), Level Zero driver
1.15.37858, SYCL backend with `GGML_SYCL_F16=ON`, graphs on. `llama-bench -ngl 99 -fa 1 -r 3`.
All models are Qwen3.8 27B variants (qwen35 architecture). "Before" is the same build with
`GGML_SYCL_ENABLE_XMX=0`. Values are tokens per second, `ppN` is a batch of N tokens, so the step
time is N / value.

| Model (GB) | tg1 | pp2 | pp4 | pp8 | pp16 | pp32 |
| Q8_0 (29.0) | 15.9 -> 18.0 | 30.6 -> 36.0 | 58.4 -> 70.7 | 108.8 -> 133 | 32.4 -> 241 | 64.3 -> 266 |
| Q6_K (22.4) | 22.8 -> 22.8 | 41 -> 44.6 | 63 -> 86 | 79 -> 159 | 45 -> 210 | n/a |
| Q4_K_S (16.4) | 26.5 -> 26.5 | 41.1 -> 48.4 | 67.7 -> 90 | 82.7 -> 131 | 50.3 -> 308 | 99 -> 354 |
| Q3_K_S (12.7) | 28.9 -> 33.1 | 27.2 -> 62 | 44.7 -> 115 | 66.6 -> 192 | 36.2 -> 243 | 71.7 -> 269 |
| Q2_K (10.8) | 33.4 -> 37.6 | 31.3 -> 69 | 50.8 -> 121 | 71.9 -> 169 | 46.6 -> 235 | 91.9 -> 266 |

End to end with speculative decoding (--spec-type draft-mtp, n-max 4, p-min 0.5, temperature 0.75, 5 prompts of 400 tokens, average tokens per second; the trim column also sets LLAMA_MTP_DRAFT_VOCAB=98304):

| Model | XMX off | XMX on | XMX on + trim |
| Q8_0 | 32.4 | 40.3 | 43.1 |
| Q4_K_S | 38.7 | 47.6 | 51.0 |
| Q3_K_S | 28.6 | 53.6 | 57.2 (63 in a later run) |
| Q2_K | 30.2 | 60.0 | 63.9 |
| Q6_K (earlier run, no p-min) | about 35 | n/a | about 55 |

Run to run noise is about 1 to 3 tokens per second on the end to end numbers (sampling).

Done:
- Each kernel was compared with the existing dp4a kernel for the same layer, on real model tensors, at 1, 2, 4, 7 and 8 columns: normalized MSE about 1e-14 for all six types (differences are float summation order only). This was done with a temporary check inside the dispatch, which is not in the tree.
- test-backend-ops test -o MUL_MAT -b SYCL0: 1132/1132 passed. NOTE: those cases use small `k` (below 1024), where the new kernel declines, so this shows no regression elsewhere but does not exercise the kernel.
- `llama-perplexity` (24 chunks of 512 tokens, text from `docs/`, `-b 32 -ub 32` so the prompt uses the kernel), Q3_K_S: 4.8360 XMX off), 4.8349 (XMX on), 4.8360 (batch 512). Q6_K, Q4_K_S and Q2_K also match within 0.003 (table at the end). Q8_0 not measured.
- Greedy generation with speculative decoding is identical for the first 1200 to 1900 characters with the kernel on or off and then diverges slightly (summation order).

Not done:
- Only one GPU model (Arc Pro B70) and one driver. Other Intel GPUs (Xe, Xe2, Arc A-series, Data Center) are untested. `load_2d`, DPAS shapes and the register file sizes are architecture dependent. The 2D block load and DPAS paths are guarded by `__has_include` only, not by a device check.
- Only qwen35 models. MoE (`MUL_MAT_ID`) is untouched. Q4_0, Q4_1, Q5_0, Q5_1, IQ types are untouched.
- `test-backend-ops` has no case that reaches the kernel (needs `k >= 1024`).
- The full local CI (ci/README.md) was not run.
- KL divergence versus a high precision reference was not measured.

## Requirements

llama_recent_prs.title: quant : extend Q8_0 to use full byte range like Q4_0 (Python+CPU)
llama_recent_prs.body:
## Overview

Mirror Q4_0 quantization logic to Q8_0, utilizing full byte range (-128~+127) for a small accurancy boost. Dequantization logic is unaffected.

This PR includes Python (`gguf-py`) and CPU backends only, per this project's one-backend-per-PR rule. I can help implement and test on the Vulkan backend after this PR is merged.

Alternative to / replaces #25493.

## Additional information

Despite the similar name, Q8_0 in it's current implementation is more "rudimentary" than Q4_0; it maps the value range to -127~+127, while Q4_0 uses a negative scaling factor trick to to use the full 4-bit range.

This PR mirrors that trick to Q8_0. By changing the scaling factor from 127 to -128, the previously unused -128 value is utilized to represent the max value in a block, while also provides finer granularity for all other values, bringing a small but real accurancy boost. This approach do, however, clamps values ranging +127.5~+128 to +127, but as the success of Q4_0 have shown us, the probability of having a value in this range is low enough that this approach brings net benefit, while not introducing too much complexity. Since the block structure is not changed in any way, dequantization logic is not affected, models created with this new approach will still be fully compatible.

Here are some test data on real-world performance (PPL and KLD). This PR cuts PPL increase by nearly half, with a negligible KLD increase. All tests are done on `wiki.test.raw` file from the Wikitext-2 dataset, obtainable via [`get-wikitext-2.sh`](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/b9957/scripts/get-wikitext-2.sh).

[Qwen3.5-0.8B](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.5-0.8B):

| - | BF16 reference | Q8_0 b9957 | Q8_0 this PR |
| - | - | - | - |
| PPL | 18.590102 | 18.628011 (+0.2039%) | 18.611565 (+0.1154%) |
| KLD | 0 (by definition) | 0.001284 | 0.001288 |

[LFM2.5-8B-A1B](https://huggingface.co/LiquidAI/LFM2.5-8B-A1B):

| - | BF16 reference | Q8_0 b9957 | Q8_0 this PR |
| - | - | - | - |
| PPL | 32.792888 | 33.271827 (+1.4605%) | 32.966434 (+0.5292%) |
| KLD | 0 (by definition) | 0.026159 | 0.026186 |

This PR is inspired by @garloff's PR #25493. His approach tries to avoid the clamping by going back to use +127 as scaling factor instead in that case. More testing and discussion is needed to compare the two approaches.

## Requirements

llama_recent_prs.title: Fix CI: gpu-metal crashes on master since #30003
llama_recent_prs.body:
## Overview

#30003 adds flash attention tests where the K and V heads have different sizes: K = 128, V = 96. Metal said it could run them, but it only has kernels when K and V are the same size, plus two special pairs, 320/256 and 576/512. So it went looking for a 128/96 kernel that doesn't exist, and test-backend-ops crashed.

Metal now only accepts the head size pairs it really has a kernel for. Anything else falls back to another backend instead of crashing. This also replaces two older partial checks with a single complete one.

Beyond the CI, this was a real Metal bug: any graph using flash attention with one of these head pairs crashed the process, it now falls back to the CPU for that op. -> Native Metal kernels for more pairs could come in a follow-up if a model needs them.

## Additional information

Tested on an M5 Max: test-backend-ops -o FLASH_ATTN_EXT passes 4675/4675 on Metal with no crash, the 128/96 cases now show as not supported, and the 320/256 and 576/512 pairs still run on Metal.

Follow-up #30003

llama_recent_prs.title: server: allow checkpoint after last media
llama_recent_prs.body:
## Overview

Allow checkpoint to be created after media so change to content after media (message) don't require reprefill of the media content.

## Additional information

Fix for #26994 .
This is easily noticeable when editing message with images in the UI, as the image on the same round get reprefill, even though UI sent image before text.

### To recreate
- Load a hybrid model (Qwen3.5/3.6) or an SWA model (Gemma 3/4) with mmproj.
- Send image + text, then the same image with different text. (with UI just edit the text)
- On the second request the image is reprocessed, see test below.

### Cause & justification
- start with #20232 as a fix for #20222 , #20726 kept the guard in place, with no checkpoint after the media, the only restore point is now before the media.
- Make sense to checkpoint the media tokens as most often it's slow and expensive to reprefill them, at the cost of an extra checkpoint.

## Changes
- is_after_last_media check for first batch follows the last media.
- Relax mid-prompt filter, the guard now only blocks checkpoints between media.

Note: The spacing rule (--checkpoint-min-step) still applies.

## Test

llama_recent_prs.title: ggml-cuda: use two-pass variance in norm_f32 to avoid NaN on constant rows with some values
llama_recent_prs.body:
## Overview

Fixes #30171 

'norm_f32 uses 'E[x^2] - E[x]^2' to find variance. When the mean is large compared to the spread, var can round to a negative value below -eps. Then rsqrtf gives NaN and the whole output row is NaN, even though the input is finite. A constant row is the simplest case. The variance is 0, so the output should be all zeros.

 

- This PR changes one-pass calculation of the variance into two-pass : first the mean and then the centered sum of squares.
- Every element in the second pass is guaranteed to be non-negative, so the variance cannot become negative. Both passes subtract a per-row shift (row's first element) so constant rows become 0. 
- '_syncthreads()' is used between two blocks because 's_sum2' is reused.

Tests added to tests\test-backend-ops.cpp
Failing before the change
```
  NORM(type=f32,ne=[768,1,1,1],v=0,eps=0.000010,noncontig_rows=0, constant=224.250000) : FAIL
  NORM(type=f32,ne=[1600,1,1,1],v=0,eps=0.000010,noncontig_rows=0, constant=22.000000) : FAIL
```


## Additional information

Clamp-only fix (`fmaxf(var, 0)`) resolved the issue in the given repro.cpp but was failing at the below offset case, which is why it wasn't used :
`NORM(type=f32,ne=[768,1,1,1],v=0,eps=0.000010,noncontig_rows=0, constant=1000.000000, spread=0.500000)`

llama_recent_prs.title: musa: Fix for FWHT shared memory bug
llama_recent_prs.body:
## Overview

#29100 broke the MUSA Docker build. The wide FWHT kernel `fwht_cuda_block<N, 256, T>` keeps a full row in a static `__shared__ float s[N]` array, so at N=8192 it needs 33300 bytes of shared memory per block. MUSA `mp_21` allows at most 28672, so both the F32 and F16 instantiations fail to compile:

```
error: shared memory (33300) exceeds limit (28672) in function '_Z15fwht_cuda_blockILi8192ELi256EfEvPKT1_Pflf'
error: shared memory (33300) exceeds limit (28672) in function '_Z15fwht_cuda_blockILi8192ELi256E6__halfEvPKT1_Pflf'
```

CUDA allows 48 KB of static shared memory by default, so CUDA builds were not affected, and the PR CI does not build MUSA.

This PR compiles the 8192 case out on MUSA. On MUSA, an 8192-wide FWHT returns false from `ggml_cuda_op_fwht_impl` and takes the existing generic fallback, the same path widths without a kernel already use (covered by the 16384 case in #29100). Widths 1024 to 4096 keep the wide kernel on MUSA; 4096 needs about 16.9 KB. CUDA and HIP are unchanged.

## Additional information

Failing job: https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/actions/runs/37727833228/job/113151497895

I don't have a MUSA toolchain, so this was not compiled for MUSA locally. I checked that preprocessing removes the 8192 case only when `GGML_USE_MUSA` is defined. @yeahdongcn, could you confirm the build on your side?

Speeds up MXFP4 MoE inference in the SYCL backend:

Arithmetic decoding is the prerequisite for the weight-reordering optimization. Other GPUs and Linux have not been tested.

llama_recent_prs.title: hexagon: fix IM2COL patch-embed DMA ring overflow
llama_recent_prs.body:
<!-- Describe what this PR does and why. Be concise but complete -->
The exact-tiling (stride == kernel, no pad/dilation) IM2COL DMA kernel issues IC*KH DDR->VTCM descriptors per output row without checking the return value of dma_queue_push(), and then pops IC*KH times. The per-thread DMA ring holds 256 entries and a push into a full ring returns false and drops the transfer, so for IC*KH > 255 the remaining rows of the VTCM staging buffer were never written and stale data (often NaN/inf) leaked into the output.

The solution is to retire the oldest descriptor when the ring is full, just as the blocked kernel in the same file already does, and wait with dma_queue_flush().

## Additional information

<!-- You can provide more details and link related discussions here. Delete this section if not applicable -->

This was found while working in stable-diffusion.cpp.

llama_recent_prs.title: graph : read recurrent states in place instead of copying (#28841)
llama_recent_prs.body:
## Overview

This is a graph only change proposed in #28841. This patch speeds up token output speed by removing the state copy steps. This does not affect anything beside the get_rows copies, as well as a new graph-reuse check and read-order changes for RWKV6/7. This change makes it so kernels that read a recurrent state now read that state directly from the cache instead of the copy, effectively removing the read and write cycle of the copy. On a 27B model that removes a 3MB read and a 3MB write per linear attention layer per token. Per token, this copy act took 209 microseconds on a 27B model, 108 microseconds on 35B-A3B, and 53 microseconds on a 0.8B model.

More concretely, recurrent and hybrid models use `llm_graph_context::build_rs` which gathers evaluation states with `ggml_get_rows(states, s_copy)`. Often, what is gathered is an identity copy. Instead of copying the identity, we can return a `ggml_view_2d` of the cache rows instead.

One change in RWKV6/7 was needed to make their graphs read token shift state before storing the new one, which is required by in-place view.

One change in delta-net-base was needed. The non-fused chunked delta-net path requires its output to be computed before the state store overwrites the old state.

This has been tested on multiple GPUs across a variety of models:

Initial tests included Qwen3.5-0.8B Q8_0, Qwen3.5-9B Q4_K_M, Qwen3.6-27B Q4_K_M, Qwen3.6-35B-A3B Q4_K_M. For a wider view other models were tested: LFM2.5 1.2B and 8B-A1B, Falcon-H1-1.5B, Granite-4.0-H-Tiny, RWKV7-0.1B.

llama_recent_prs.title: llama : fix unexpected graph reallocation in the k-pool models
llama_recent_prs.body:
## Overview

The k-pool models built their graph shape from state the full-context reserve cannot know, so the first decode with a different shape forced a scheduler re-reserve that dropped the worst-case sizing; the next state growth then needed more room at an unchanged graph size and aborted under `GGML_SCHED_DEBUG_REALLOC=1`.

Two branches caused it:

- `qwen4exp` branched on `inp->cache_safe`, which turns false as soon as `llama_memory_seq_cp` shares cells (e.g. `llama-batched-bench -pps`): the 12 QSA layers swapped scatter+gather for fill+concat and dropped the `new_pool_rep` leaf, so the decode graph had 12 fewer nodes and one fewer leaf than the reserved one
- `glm5-next` branched on `gather = n_tokens <= 16 && n_kv > n_sel`, so a TG decode built the gather shape (7564 nodes) while the last reserve, the PP one, had the dense shape (7762 nodes)

The fix makes the shape constant per context:

- `qwen4exp` and `glm5-next` always create `new_pool_rep` and always scatter the fresh pooled keys before gathering all `n_pool` of them by cell; without sharing every pool is re-pooled anyway (`n_new == n_pool_real`, layout order), so `new_pool_rep[ip] == pool_cells[ip]` and the gather returns exactly what the removed concat produced for every visible pool, while padded pools stay `-inf` masked as before
- `glm5-next` picks `gather` from context constants: `cparams.n_ubatch` bounds every ubatch, `top_k + kpool - 1` bounds `n_sel`, so the shape follows neither `n_tokens` nor `n_kv`
- `set_input_kpool` now requires `new_pool_rep`, and the dead `get_kpool_cache_safe()` API plus the unread `cache_safe` copy in `kpool_build_sizes()` are gone

## Additional information

Repro, aborts before this PR:

    GGML_SCHED_DEBUG_REALLOC=1 ./bin/llama-batched-bench -hf ggml-org/GLM-5.3-Flash-GGUF:Q2_K -npp 2500 -ntg 32 -npl 1,2 -c 32768 -pps -kvu

    ggml_backend_sched_alloc_splits: unexpected graph reallocation (graph size = 8116, nodes = 8116, leafs = 1520), debug_realloc = 1

Verified after the change, all exit 0: the command above, the same with `-npp 512`, with `-ub 16` (exercises the gather shape, all graphs 7564 nodes), the qwen4exp equivalent, plus `test-llama-archs` (502) and `test-recurrent-state-rollback` / `test-save-load-state` / `test-opt`, all under `GGML_SCHED_DEBUG_REALLOC=1`. Reserves and every decode now share one node count per context, so no decode-time re-reserve happens any more.

The dense path also measured faster than the gather path on Apple M2 Ultra, so the constant choice costs nothing: at 16k context PP/TG are 259/23.9 t/s dense vs 110/21.6 t/s gather, at 2.5k context 284/24.4 vs 273/21.5.

## Requirements

- I have read and agree with the [contributing guidelines](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- AI usage disclosure: YES. pi:llama.cpp/MiMo-V2.6-Flash-MOPD

llama_recent_prs.title: Add SYCL graph record and replay
llama_recent_prs.body: ## Overview This is a port of the existing CUDA graph code to SYCL. The code is mostly a straight port with two SYCL-specific exceptions: 1. The data must be reordered before recording because while SYCL async memory allocation extensions are available, using them leads to a hang during graph recording. 2. The library GEMM functions don't work with graph recording because it throws an exception: "Graph nodes cannot depend on events from outside the graph." This effectively limits the feature to decode for the time being. On A770 the performance improvement during decode is significant; on B70 it is negligible. Thus the feature remains off by default. ## Additional information While investigating performance differences on A770 between the Vulkan and SYCL backends, I found that kernel dispatch time consumed a large percentage of the SYCL time. llama_recent_prs.title: vulkan: Add workaround for device free memory > total memory on Intel Windows
llama_recent_prs.body:
## Overview

Fixes #29277 by calculating free memory based on the smaller value of `heapBudget` or `VkMemoryHeap::size`.

Tested on i7-1270P with graphics driver 32.0.101.7085, 40GB RAM, running Windows 11 25H2 10.0.26200.9448
### Before (32dd62ee)
```
λ .\build_vk\bin\Debug\test-backend-ops.exe -b Vulkan0 -o ADD(type=f16,ne=[1,1,8,1],nr=[1,1,1,1],nf=1,perm1=0,src_overlap=0)
ggml_vulkan: Found 1 Vulkan devices:
ggml_vulkan: 0 = Intel(R) Iris(R) Xe Graphics (Intel Corporation) | uma: 1 | fp16: 1 | bf16: 0 | fp4: 0 | warp size: 32 | shared memory: 32768 | int dot: 1 | matrix cores: none
...
Backend 1/2: Vulkan0
  Device description: Intel(R) Iris(R) Xe Graphics
  Device memory: 20312 MB (23473 MB free)
...
```

### After (1fc772a)
```
λ .\build_vk\bin\Debug\test-backend-ops.exe -b Vulkan0 -o ADD(type=f16,ne=[1,1,8,1],nr=[1,1,1,1],nf=1,perm1=0,src_overlap=0)
ggml_vulkan: Found 1 Vulkan devices:
ggml_vulkan: 0 = Intel(R) Iris(R) Xe Graphics (Intel Corporation) | uma: 1 | fp16: 1 | bf16: 0 | fp4: 0 | warp size: 32 | shared memory: 32768 | int dot: 1 | matrix cores: none
...
Backend 1/2: Vulkan0
  Device description: Intel(R) Iris(R) Xe Graphics
  Device memory: 20312 MB (20312 MB free)
...
```

## Additional information
There was a behavior change deployed in recent Windows where [Shared GPU memory size is calculated as](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-hardware/drivers/display/calculating-graphics-memory) `TotalSystemMemoryAvailableForGraphics = MIN((TotalSystemMemory * 80%), MAX((TotalSystemMemory - 16GB), (TotalSystemMemory * 50%))`, while previously it was (typically) 50% of system memory. This behavior change seems to affect the Windows Vulkan driver causing `VkMemoryHeap::size` to be smaller than `heapBudget` on systems with large RAM.

At the moment, `VkMemoryHeap::size` seems to follow the settings of [Shared GPU Memory Override](https://www.intel.com/content/www/us/en/support/articles/000101789/graphics.html). Users may want to try changing the setting to match the Windows default Shared GPU memory size to improve iGPU memory utilization.

llama_recent_prs.title: vulkan: query-row slicing for large-batch flash attention at deep KV
llama_recent_prs.body:
## Overview This PR improves deep-context Vulkan prefill on RDNA3 by splitting flash-attention dispatches into serialized slices of 512 query rows. Shader math and tile geometry stay unchanged, and other operations retain the full ubatch. Slicing requires more than 512 query rows, KV ≥ 12288, and plain dense attention without GQA rewriting, sparse attention, or split-K. Decode is unaffected; the device gate enables RDNA3 only. ## Benchmark Summary - AMD Radeon PRO W7800 48 GB, `gfx1100` / RDNA3 - RADV / Mesa `26.0.8-1ubuntu0.3`, Vulkan `1.4.335`, kernel `7.0.0-34-generic` - Upstream `c811cb8f0` → final revision `a5bda10ea`; `A-B-B-A`, `-r 3`, means of the two arms per side - `-ngl 999 -t 4 -sm none -b 2048 -ctk f16 -ctv f16 -fa on`

llama_recent_prs.title: server: skip context checkpoints and state saves for cache_prompt=false tasks
llama_recent_prs.body:
## Overview

This PR skips automatic RAM prompt-cache saves and prompt-reuse checkpoints for `cache_prompt = false` tasks. It avoids checkpoint copies and extra ubatches on recurrent, hybrid, and SWA models, and skips automatic cache saves on other models too. Both LRU and idle-slot saves respect the task's caching policy. Requests with `cache_prompt = true`, live-prefix reuse, and explicit slot saves remain supported; explicitly restored state becomes cacheable again.

## Benchmark Summary

- AMD Radeon PRO W7800 48 GB, `gfx1100` / RDNA3; Vulkan, RADV / Mesa `26.0.8-1ubuntu0.3`
- Qwen3.8 27B Q8_0 hybrid + MTP Q4_0 draft
- `--ctx-size 32768 --cache-ram 20480 -b 2048 -ub 2048 --parallel 1`
- `-ctk f16 -ctv f16 --flash-attn on --spec-type draft-mtp --spec-draft-n-max 3`
- Upstream `c811cb8f0` versus final revision `96e1d229f`, including the restore fix; `A-B-B-A`
- Per binary: 60 no-cache probes (13 tokens, `n_predict = 1`) and 12 following cache-enabled requests with unique 1.4–1.9k-token prompts; no cache hits

| Measurement | Baseline | Candidate |
|---|---:|---:|
| Probe prompt time, p50 | 269.5 ms | 107.7 ms (-60.0%) |

llama_recent_prs.title: grammar: accept tool-call argument properties in any order - #1
llama_recent_prs.body:
Tool-call argument grammars built from a tool's JSON schema enforce the declared property order. When a model writes the keys in a different order (Nemotron-3 Super writes dtype before expr, schema lists expr first), the grammar masks the key it wants and sampling produces garbage keys such as expr\": or drops the field.

## Overview
Opt-in unordered object mode in the schema-to-grammar converter, enabled for tool-call argument schemas only (`tool_args` / `tool_arg_json_value`).

* Required keys: exactly once, in any order (2^n rules). With more than 6 required keys the declared order is kept.
* Optional keys: anywhere, in any order. They may repeat. **This is a side effect**
   *  Allowing any order while still rejecting repeats means the grammar must track which keys were already written, which takes 2^n rules for n keys. That is fine for the few required keys a tool usually has, but not for schemas with many optional keys (the 14-property column-like object would need 16384 rules). Capping the tracked keys and keeping the declared order above the cap would bring back the original bug for exactly those schemas, so only required keys are tracked. 
* Additional keys: anywhere, unbounded as before.
* `--json-schema` and response-format grammars are unchanged. Parsing of model output is unchanged.


Behavior change to be aware of: duplicate optional declared keys are now accepted (upstream rejects them). Duplicate JSON keys are parsed differently by different consumers (most keep the last value, strict parsers may error); the cap bounds runaway repetition.

## Additional information

Measured on Nemotron-3-Super-120B UD-Q6_K, temperature 1.0, 32 requests each (complete = no corrupt keys, required fields present).

| request | before | with fix |
|---|---|---|
| full tool-calling request | 27/32 | 32/32 |
| minimal repro (original schema order) | 2/32 | 32/32 |

llama_recent_prs.title: vulkan: add tiled concat for transposed inputs
llama_recent_prs.body:
## Overview This PR adds `concat_transpose.comp`, a 32x32 LDS-tiled Vulkan shader for the dim-0 concat that several recurrent architectures build in each of their recurrent layers: `conv_input = concat(conv_state, transpose(qkv_mixed), 0)`. The existing flat concat shader walks that concat along `i0` and reads the transposed input with a row-sized lane stride, so each lane of a wave touches a different cache line. With `GGML_VK_PERF_LOGGER` on Qwen3.8 27B Q8_0 (48 recurrent layers) during the initial evaluation, the 48 CONCAT nodes per ubatch took 122 ms of a 2.97 s prefill chunk at ubatch 2048. The tiled shader uses the same scheme as `copy_transpose.comp`: loads follow `src1`'s contiguous dimension, stores follow the destination's contiguous dimension. It is selected only for dim-0, non-quantized 4-byte concat where `src1` is a transposed view, at least 32 elements wide, and no narrower than `src0`; every other concat keeps the flat shader. On a Radeon PRO W7800 / gfx1100 with RADV Mesa 26.0.8, the gain grows with ubatch: +1.0% (dense) and +1.6% (MoE) at pp2048/ub512, +3.2% and +7.6% at pp2048/ub2048, and +4.9% and +11.1% at pp4096/pp8192 with ubatch 4096. A control model without this concat shape is unchanged. Measured only on gfx1100 / RADV. The tiled path is only selected for 4-byte non-quantized concat, so quantized types are out of scope by construction. ## Benchmark Summary Hardware/software: - AMD Radeon PRO W7800 48 GB (`gfx1100` / RDNA3) - RADV / Mesa `26.0.8-1ubuntu0.3`, Vulkan API 1.4.335, kernel `7.0.0-34-generic` - master `b9acf138a` vs master + this PR (two binaries) - `llama-bench -p 512/2048/4096/8192 -n 0 -fa on -ctk f16 -ctv f16 -ngl 999 -t 12 -r 3`; batch = ubatch per row; A-B-B-A per cell ```text fires on: dim-0 concat, non-quantized 4-byte type, src1 a transposed view (nb[1] == type_size, nb[0] >= ne1 * nb[1]), src1->ne[0] >= 32 and src1->ne[0] >= src0->ne[0] ```

## Overview

<!-- Describe what this PR does and why. Be concise but complete -->

Eleven independent fixes:

- q4_K split-K decode GEMV and the generic GEMVs: clamp the row tail and the weight-fetch row to the tensor
  (out-of-bounds reads at rows not a multiple of the tile).
- Decline weights the transposed Adreno layout cannot represent (rows not a multiple of 4 aborted the backend).
- Keep vocab-scale q4_K weights off an image path larger than the device can hold.
- Keep q4_0 weights already in the bin layout out of the quant-to-f16 reroute.
- Flash attention: apply the logit softcap before the mask, as ggml does (fixes the large-logits softcap case on  every Adreno).

Use 64-bit arithmetic for the destination offsets in both store paths of kernel_mul_mm. This stops mistakes from happening when those offsets are above the signed 32-bit range.

llama_recent_prs.title: opencl: perf optimization for mamba2 ssm_scan by folding 4 dim rows into one workgroup and add more coverage
llama_recent_prs.body:
## Overview

<!-- Describe what this PR does and why. Be concise but complete -->

Two changes to the mamba2 `ssm_scan` kernel from #26439.

**Optimization: fewer redundant loads.** B and C are indexed by `(group, token)`, never by `dim`, but the kernel runs one work-group per `(head, dim)` row, so hundreds of work-groups re-read the same values every token. Folding `SSM_R` consecutive rows into one work-group loads them once. `SSM_R` is compile-time so the row loop unrolls and the state stays in registers; `SSM_R=1` is the original kernel unchanged. Used when `d_state == 128` and `head_dim % 4 == 0`, otherwise the one-row kernel. Improve a third of prefill perf on an all-mamba2 model; `GGML_OPENCL_SSM_ROWS=1` opts out.

**Converage: rollback snapshots on the GPU.** The kernel wrote only the final recurrent state, so `supports_op` declined every `K > 1` and each SSM layer of a speculative verify fell to the CPU. It now writes slots `1..K-1` in the token loop. `test-backend-ops -o SSM_SCAN` goes from 6/6 to 7/7 on Adreno 840 and 740.
